killed: **The 2026-11-13 paid GA date and the 'three months free' founding term.** Killed by the money critic: `trial_period_days` is set nowhere so the term was never implemented, and three months from mid-November lands the first charge in mid-February against Census MARTS medians of Jan 0.913 / Feb 0.917 — the second-worst cash month of the restaurant year. A locked launch date with no billing engine behind it is a promise the company cannot keep, on a date it chose badly.

**The $19/location founding rate and the Solo/Team/Accountant tiers.** Killed by their own registry: `pricing-constants.ts` marks founding `billable: false` — no SKU, no `priceIdForTier` branch, no `STRIPE_PRICE_*` field — while Solo ($25) and Team ($60) are `per_account` with no location cap, so a three-location founding member pays $57 against an unlimited-location $25 tier, and the posted 150-invoice Solo cap is enforced nowhere. Five posted prices, zero coherent, one billable. Replaced by one price and, for the first cohort, no billing code at all.

**The bookkeeper CHANNEL — the Accountant tier, `hasCockpit: true`, the never-built /cockpit route, and the `firms` entity rebuild.** Killed by the bookkeeper attack: the cockpit is architecturally forbidden today (`/switch` sets a cookie whose own comment says every request re-resolves to exactly ONE org under RLS), the prerequisite `firms` entity appears zero times in that plan's own 90 days, the day-one posting path synthesizes its extraction from an `x-muntin-extraction` request header and dry-runs by default, and MarginEdge shipped an accountant-specific product in 2023. The CODE survives as the exception desk's internal tool; the channel is deferred, not built.

**The Muntin Reference Plate.** Killed by the unit census: 70 of 82 shipping references are carton/sack/dozen, `portion-bridge.js` UNIT_FAMILIES contains none of them so `unitsCompatible` returns false, no series.json carries a package descriptor, and `data/cost-plate-drift.json` already tried this and excluded every non-per-lb item as non-bridgeable. A stipulated pack weight is not a free stipulation; it is an unrecorded property of the source quote, and asserting one is the exact invention the fact gate exists to forbid.

**The attestation product ($250/statement, $2,400/yr).** Killed twice: the substrate is `data/cost-index-editions.json`, which holds four editions (two reconstructed seeds) and has been written to exactly ONCE in 348 commits — it can certify two real dates; and the storefront repo is PUBLIC, so every frozen edition already sits in a git history where the commit SHA is a content hash with an author date. Muntin would be charging for a first-party letter about what Muntin published, weaker than the free public proof it duplicates.

**The paid Lock List and the 'priceable enough to commit' headline.** Killed by the calibration file: `lockMinCoverageLo = 0.60` admits an item to 'Lock' when the lower bound of realized coverage merely clears 60% against an 0.80 nominal band, 36 of 37 Lock items realize below nominal, and `overallHitRate` is 0.506 against a 0.502 baseline over 34,029 calls. That is a directional commit recommendation wearing a risk-word costume, from a company that permanently foreclosed direction claims. Monetizing it at $588/yr is the honesty fence broken at the load-bearing point.

**The vendor-rep Market Sheet distribution experiment as designed.** Killed on two counts the proposal never names: Don is FOH, not the buyer — the rep calls on the owner/chef, so the experiment is contaminated even if it runs — and it routes a personal company's sales test through the employer's vendor relationships. Also killed on substrate: the frozen-edition spine the sheet must cite is 32 days stale while the live read is 2 days old, so the proposal's own provenance gate would mandate the stale number.

**Any public `no-llm-ci.sh` falsification command, until the script is publicly executable.** Killed by repo visibility: the script lives only in `Muntin-Invoice-Decoder`, which is PRIVATE. Four separate proposals print 'here is the command a stranger can run' on a public page. Printing an unrunnable proof on the one object whose entire purpose is being checked is the single failure this brand cannot survive. The claim stays; the fake invitation goes.

**Publishing Tacombi's real September in full, forever, publicly.** My own kill, and the largest unnamed flaw in the winning bet — zero of six proposals contain the words authorization, consent, or employer. A full month of an employer's AP and food cost, with vendor names and negotiated prices, published permanently by an employee to sell his own company, is a confidentiality breach and plausibly a firing offense. Replaced by: written authorization from ownership, or a redacted specimen, or a consenting third restaurant.

**Traffic as an objective, list growth as a metric, site-wide analytics ambition, and site-wide EN↔ES parity as a ratchet.** Killed by the arithmetic of the winning model: 40 customers ever needs ~400 qualified readers, not 400,000. 274 of 1,327 pages emit analytics — instrument the ~50 a qualified buyer touches and stop pretending to measure the other 1,277. The ES funnel is dead at every terminus (2 of 651 ES pages carry a waitlist, 1 of 384 ES subscribe boxes emits a mailable source, zero ES dispatch editions exist), so parity is scoped to `/es/cost-index/` and the rest freezes. The Spanish 24-hour reply and phone-callback SLA in `copy.es.ts:2521,2532,2538` comes down today — it is an uncosted promise from a company with no artifact establishing conversational Spanish.

**The audio pipeline for all new work, and per-invoice / percentage-of-savings pricing.** Audio: 114 rendered tracks and an ≥80-char `data-audio-alt` obligation enforced in CI on every new figure; no $600 buyer has ever asked for narrated prose. Freeze the manifest, add nothing. Pricing: variable cost is ~half a cent per document against competitors whose COGS is a model call per document, so flat-rate is the one structural advantage they cannot copy; and `fair-price-gap.js` already states on the record that wholesale data alone cannot prove overpayment, so the product cannot bill on a saving it cannot measure. Both foreclosed in an ADR so no future session reproposes them.

**The operator-submitter data lane.** Killed pre-emptively while killing it is still free (vindication-instrument's sharpest permanent move): accepting operator-submitted prices converts the index's one growth mechanism into a permanent, undelegatable founder moderation queue and destroys the public-source provenance that makes the archive unfabricatable. Foreclosed in an ADR now, not argued about later.

ranked.bet: Price inversion — sell a signed monthly close at ~$600/location, ~40 locations, correctness as the product
ranked.verdict: ADOPT AS SPINE, with three mandatory repairs
ranked.why: It is the only bet that passes all three standing critics. CAPACITY: its revenue model is the only one not founder-hours-linear in acquisition — 40 customers ever, not 100+ subscribers — and it computes its own one-founder ceiling out loud (≈20 founder-minutes of close review × 40 locations = 13.3 h/month against 13-26 available, $288K ARR, described as a very good one-person business rather than dressed up as a venture). Its explicit founder budget is ~15.5 hours across 90 days, the tightest-fitting of the six, and the hours are concentrated in things only the founder can do. HONESTY: it is the only bet that pays the correctness debt BEFORE opening any channel, and the only one whose refusal clause is the right refusal — 'ship the close before the legs foot' is the thing it will not do to save itself. Every other bet defers, gates, or withholds the defective number and then sells something adjacent to it; this one fixes it and charges for the fix. FIRST DOLLAR: it prices at the one band with demonstrated evidence — independents pay $350-500/location for a measured food-cost number — and is the only bet selling exactly the object that evidence is evidence for. At $7,200/yr per location, three founder-hours to close a customer is trivially affordable, which is precisely the acquisition motion $19 made impossible. The three repairs are non-negotiable: employer authorization before any real invoice is published, hand-invoicing instead of a billing rebuild, and the founder walk moved to week one.

ranked.bet: The Index IS the company — Michelin, inverted
ranked.verdict: KILL AS STRATEGY — HARVEST ITEM 4 AND THE LABOUR DOCTRINE
ranked.why: The strategic reframe is correct and survives into the winner: selling labour over data that stays free removes billing.ts, the missing SKU, `stripe_subscriptions.org_id`, the phantom /cockpit route and the GA date from the critical path, and 5 buyers at $400/mo beats 105 at $228/yr. But the bet is fatal on its own premise. It says what the index lacks is 'citation capture, not rigor' while `cost-index/feed.json` publishes a BLS index value as a $393.06/lb wholesale price and `index.json` prints $5.51/lb for the same slug — two published surfaces disagreeing by 71× — and the gate written to catch exactly that passes because it checks the ingredient's best available level, not the basis of the rendered observation. Every one of its twelve moves (164 embed cards, a DOI, a press kit, a CC0 grant) amplifies that artifact. Its headline noun is a false license claim the repo already decided against (ADR-015/017: gov passthroughs CC0, Muntin compilations CC BY), its flagship Reference Plate is unbuildable, and its own #1 move is arithmetically wrong (CAP=90 silently drops 685 of 775 and stamps the edition delivered). It is the clearest case in the audit of opening a channel before the thing that channel inspects is correct.

ranked.bet: Sell to the bookkeeper; the restaurants come free
ranked.verdict: DEFER THE CHANNEL — HARVEST THE LIMITS REGISTER AND THE READINESS DISCIPLINE
ranked.why: The discovery is real and nobody had named it: Muntin spent a year building an accounting-firm product — five bookkeeper queues, statement reconciliation, GL rules, signed Ed25519 workpapers, 3,665 lines of QBO/Xero, and the ONLY tier in the codebase with both `billable: true` and a live Stripe price-ID branch — and has never told a firm, while 4 of 1,327 pages carry a waitlist aimed at an owner who signs no cheque. The measurement is the most accurate in the audit. But the readiness claim is false at the line level: the day-one product is `posting.ts`, which synthesizes its extraction from a request header, returns 'Unknown vendor' on fallback and dry-runs by default. The cockpit is forbidden by per-request single-org RLS resolution, and the `firms` entity that would unforbid it is scheduled zero times. $39/client is 2.2× the Dext anchor for strictly less than Dext delivers once the identity is withheld. And the correctness firewall does not hold — credit memos and catch-weight are AP defects, found in the first bank reconciliation, not in the food-cost tab. Right buyer, twelve months early. The firm becomes a referral source and a CPA reviewer in Phase 2, not a customer.

ranked.bet: The open institution — credibility as the entire moat
ranked.verdict: HARVEST THE PUBLIC-RECORD LAYER AND THE DOCTRINE — KILL THE FUNDING MODEL
ranked.why: Its central doctrinal insight is the one that resolves the founder's sequencing question and I am adopting it wholesale: credibility is a CLOSING asset, not a demand asset. That single sentence explains why every 'amplify the index' bet fails and why the storefront's job changes from acquisition to qualification. Its measurements of the storefront's state reproduce exactly, and its refusals/freshness/calibration surfaces are the cheapest confidence artifacts available because they are already computed (100 pre-written `toHigh` blockers, 42 written coverage gaps). But the funding architecture bolted on top is unfundable. The attestation lane — its own designated wedge — has a substrate of two certifiable dates and sells a first-party letter about facts already free in a public git history. The pricing section misses its own headline multiple by 10× ('17×' for 1.71×) and its own headline sum by $900, in a document whose thesis is that this is the party that publishes its own error rate. And 76 transactions in the proof year are budgeted zero founder sales hours against ~95 needed. Doctrine survives; product dies.

ranked.bet: The vindication instrument — standing in front of the vendor rep
ranked.verdict: KILL THE INSTRUMENT — SHIP THE DEAD ENGINES AND THE SUBMITTER-LANE ADR
ranked.why: Five of its calls are correct and three survive into the winner: do not launch food-cost until the four named defects are paid ('a number biased low three ways is the one number an evidence brand cannot print'), do not build the bookkeeper channel, and never build the operator-submitter lane. But the instrument itself is unshippable. Its flagship proof is `no-llm-ci.sh`, which lives in the private repo and cannot be run by the stranger it is printed for. Its own new provenance gate would force the sheet to cite a 32-day-stale edition spine while a 2-day-old read sits one file away — and the plan simultaneously retires the only wired alarm that fires when the spine stops advancing. The price is derived by reading a $25/week noise-suppression threshold as delivered value, from a file whose own header says 'the email never prints it,' and it raises price 4.2× while cutting the deliverable the price comparison rests on. What survives is its best paragraph: five honesty-gated tools sitting on disk, referenced by zero of 1,327 pages, that visibly DECLINE to speak when the evidence is inconclusive — executable proof a stranger can run in a browser with no repo access, which is exactly what the private script can never be.

ranked.bet: Radical narrowing — one number, one surface, one job
ranked.verdict: HARVEST THE FOUNDER WALK AND THE PROVABLY-DEAD CUT — REJECT THE HEADLINE AND THE AMPUTATION
ranked.why: Its diagnosis is the most physically true statement in the audit — a one-person company cannot defend 1,327 promises, and ~53 obligation-hours against 13-26 available at ~10% realized payment makes that a fact, not an opinion. And it contains the single most valuable four hours in the entire material: the founder running 20 real invoices through his own product and writing down every place it lied. But the execution inverts its own logic. It schedules that walk eleventh of twelve, AFTER deleting the count/inventory feature it is meant to authorize, and its own text concedes the walk could send it back to the identity 'despite everything above.' Its cut list breaks `cost-watch-scan.ts`, which imports four deleted modules and feeds the only dollar figure the product can honestly print. Its headline is a directional lock recommendation admitted at 0.60 against an 0.80 nominal. Its founder estimates are not credible (72 published corrections in 3 hours = 2.5 minutes each; 260 permanent route deletions in 1 hour = 14 seconds each). And nothing in it ships, because the red deploy it names in 'How It Fails' is never cleared in the plan.

reasoning: Six bets, five of them fatal under blind attack, and the sixth — price inversion — carrying one fatal flaw that no attacker was assigned to find and that I found myself. I weighted the three standing critics as instructed and they converge unusually cleanly. On capacity: five of six bets need volume (775 subscribers, 100 firms, 40 memberships, 10 pilot restaurants plus a paid newsletter), and every volume path routes through founder-hours the ledger says do not exist — ~53 h/month of obligation against 13-26 available with roughly 10% actually paid in the last 30 days. Price inversion is the only bet whose acquisition math shrinks with price rather than growing with it, and the only one that writes its own ceiling down honestly ($288K, one founder, forty locations, not a venture). On the honesty fence: the storefront currently publishes a BLS index value as a $393.06/lb wholesale price, 72 live falsehoods on the flagship post, a citation drawer inviting a skeptic to verify against a CI gate that was never written, and a public claim to a falsification command that lives in a private repo — and four of the six bets propose to amplify reach across exactly those surfaces. Price inversion is the only bet whose first act is to make the number true rather than to make it louder. On first dollar: $228/yr forecloses every human-touch channel, which is why every cheap-price bet ends up needing a channel it cannot afford or a schema it has not scheduled; $7,200/yr per location buys the direct channel back, and it is the only price in the material anchored to demonstrated willingness-to-pay for the exact object being sold. That resolves the sequencing question the brief posed, and I want to state the answer plainly rather than hedge it: correctness comes first, and the founder's wish for traffic now is the wrong objective, not merely a mistimed one. At forty customers ever the storefront needs roughly four hundred qualified readers, not four hundred thousand visits — so amplifying reach is not just risky, it is spending scarce hours on a metric the business model does not consume. The genuine consolation is that the confidence move and the only durable traffic move are the same move: the 306 cost-index pages are the appreciating asset an answer engine must re-fetch because the numbers change, and correcting them, publishing the corrections ledger, the refusals page and the calibration record is simultaneously what makes a CPA trust the close and what keeps the index citable. Only vanity traffic is sacrificed, and the ~460 pages of explanatory prose being frozen are depreciating in precisely the category AI eats. The buyer this company can afford — the owner with a bookkeeper champion, and the CPA who reviews the close — is also the reader most likely to catch a food-cost percentage biased low three ways, which makes amplify-then-fix not a risk but a scheduled credibility event. I am also killing one thing the winning bet proposed and every proposal missed: publishing Tacombi's complete September, with vendor names and negotiated prices, permanently and publicly, by an employee, to sell his own company. Zero of six documents contain the words authorization, consent, or employer, and that omission is more dangerous than any pricing error in the material. Finally, this decision has to abandon things, because a company that has retired exactly one subsystem in fifteen months and only because a gate forced it does not get credit for a plan that adds. Five posted prices, a locked GA date, a channel, a data product, a headline, a language parity ratchet, an audio pipeline and a growth mechanism all die here, and the retirement pass rides under a one-in-one-out gate enforced by machinery rather than by a policy line in a file that loads in 1 of 108 sessions.
synthesis: **From index-is-the-company — the src-sentinel and corrections program, grafted whole and moved to Phase 0.** Correct the July dispatch in place, repoint all 165 `<!-- src: -->` annotations at the frozen `data/cost-index-editions.json` snapshot, write and wire `scripts/check-src-sentinel.mjs`, and ship an append-only `/cost-index/corrections/` where every entry names the gate that now prevents recurrence. This survives because it is the only move in the entire audit that makes the instrument MORE CORRECT rather than louder, and because the defect it fixes is live and brand-threatening: 72 published claims are currently false, and line 852 tells a reader those files are 're-checked in CI' when no such gate exists on disk, on a public repo, with a revision count off by 5×. It costs almost no founder hours, it converts an unenforced prose convention into a machine-checked one, and under the winning bet it is the storefront's confidence spine rather than a citation-capture play.

**From index-is-the-company — the labour-over-free-data doctrine, as the second SKU only.** The methodology page forecloses placement and influence, not analysis, service or expertise; a paid cost review in Don's own voice over data that stays free and CC0 is fully sellable. This survives as the natural adjacency AFTER one close is proven, and it dies as a primary revenue line for the reason the attack found: judgment and relationship are the two things the agent workforce cannot supply, so five Reference Desk clients at four hours each consume the entire monthly budget and success becomes the failure mode.

**From bookkeeper-platform — the append-only, code-cited known-limits register, published as `/close/limits/`.** Every defect entered with file and line, maintained as a by-product of the fix commits, never retroactively edited. This survives on three grounds: it is fact-gate-safe by construction because every line cites a file rather than a market claim; it is the exact shape of the 10,294-entry revisions ledger, the one ritual this company has never let lapse; and under a $600 close it stops being an apology and becomes the artifact the price is justified by — the CPA reads it before recommending you, and it is the document nobody else in the category publishes.

**From bookkeeper-platform — the readiness discipline, generalized into a rule.** 'Before any pitch, prove one real invoice posts end-to-end' becomes 'nothing is sold, priced, or published until one correct close exists.' This survives because it is the specific antidote to how that bet died: it audited its own product by line count (444/909/955/3665, all exact) and inferred function from size, never running the bytes against real data. The winning bet's Phase 0 founder walk is the same discipline applied to the identity rather than to the posting path.

**From bookkeeper-platform — the firm as referral source and reviewer, not as customer.** The five bookkeeper queues, statement reconciliation, GL rules and signed Ed25519 workpaper export stop being an unmarketed customer surface and become the exception desk's internal tool, while two working restaurant CPAs review the specimen close. This survives because it captures the entire real asset of that bet — the accounting-firm code and the accounting-firm relationship — at zero cost, without the `firms` entity, the RLS rewrite, the billing inversion, or a bet against a competitor three years ahead.

**From vindication-instrument — the dead engines shipped as `/tools/pack-check/`.** `pack-shrink.js` (which refuses to say 'shrink' unless the per-base jump clears 5% with the sticker quiet inside 2%), `vendor-ask.js` (which withholds the entire card when the decomposition is inconclusive), `vendor-switch.js`, `silent-bleed.js` and `url-fragment.js` are on disk, parity-locked to the product's TypeScript, EN+ES, honesty-gated, and referenced by zero of 1,327 pages. They survive as the storefront's PUBLIC falsifier, replacing the unrunnable `no-llm-ci.sh` command: a tool that visibly declines to speak is a stronger honesty proof than the 89 pages that merely claim honesty, and a stranger can run it in a browser with no repo access — which is precisely what a script in a private repo can never be. One to two agent sessions, no new gate, no price change, no founder signature beyond approving a page of copy.

**From vindication-instrument — the ADR foreclosing the operator-submitter lane, written now while writing it is free.** Survives because the SOFR/LIBOR reasoning is correct and because this is the one growth mechanism that converts directly into a permanent, undelegatable founder moderation queue in a company already 2.7× oversubscribed. Closing a door costs nothing today and costs everything after the first submission arrives.

**From radical-narrowing — the twenty-invoice founder walk, promoted from eleventh to FIRST.** Four to six founder-hours converting the load-bearing assumption of the entire company from a hope into a measured fact, with four recorded numbers: minutes the count actually took, share of invoice DOLLARS surviving into a valued Purchases leg, rows landing in `needs_review`, and whether the legs footed. It survives and gets promoted because every independent critic named it the most valuable item in the material, because no agent session can substitute for it, and because it attacks the root fact that after fifteen months the founder has never run his own product once. Below ~70% dollar survival, the pilot does not open and the quarter is saved.

**From radical-narrowing — the provably-dead cut as the only Phase-0 deletion.** 162 dead-weight pages that are already frozen AND already orphaned: no crawler sees them, no internal link leads to them. Survives because it is the one deletion that risks nothing and needs no traffic data — but it is explicitly NOT counted as the retirement, because retiring what nothing reaches retires zero obligation. That honest accounting is itself grafted: it is the difference between motion and closure that produced a 26% audit-close rate.

**From open-institution — 'credibility is a closing asset, not a demand asset,' adopted as positioning doctrine.** This is the sentence that resolves the founder's sequencing question. Under it the storefront's job flips from acquisition to qualification: ~400 qualified readers ever, ~50 instrumented pages, an application rather than a waitlist. It survives because it is the general principle behind every specific failure in this audit — five bets tried to convert credibility into demand, and credibility does not do that; it converts consideration into signature.

**From open-institution — `/cost-index/refusals/` and `/cost-index/freshness/`, built from data already computed.** The 100 pre-written `toHigh` blocker strings in `data/cost-index-health.json` and the 42 written structural gap reasons in `data/cost-index.json#coverage.gaps` become the public record of what Muntin will not say and why. Survives because publishing your refusals is the cheapest confidence artifact available (the strings exist; nobody has to write them), because it is the same negative-results instinct the specimen close applies to the product, and because it makes `highEligible: 0` a disclosed fact rather than a discoverable one.

**From open-institution — get the live fetch off the founder's Mac.** One founder session putting FRED_KEY / BLS_KEY / AMS_KEY into GitHub Actions secrets so the refresh workflow appends editions instead of silently exiting 0. Survives as the highest-value single founder hour in the material after the walk: it is the only move no agent can execute, it protects the sole unfabricatable asset (2,025 live-captured points and a dated publication chain), and 26 series are already frozen 58-77 days against a 120-day drop cliff. A read-only government data key is not a real credential boundary.

**MY OWN GRAFT, non-negotiable — written authorization before any employer data is published, and a redacted or third-party specimen.** Zero of six proposals contain the words authorization, consent, or employer, while the winning bet proposes publishing Tacombi's complete September — vendor names, negotiated prices, food cost — permanently and publicly, signed, by an employee, to sell his own company. The specimen close ships only under one of three conditions: written authorization from ownership, a redaction that generalizes vendor identity and contract prices, or a consenting third restaurant. The same rule retroactively covers the seven real invoice fixtures committed under an MIT LICENSE in the private product repo — a hygiene problem today, an incident the moment that repo opens.

**MY OWN GRAFT — no billing code for the first cohort.** Ten to forty customers ever do not need a Stripe SKU, a checkout surface, a `priceIdForTier` branch or a per-location quantity source. They need an invoice, sent by hand, annually, in the May-August peak. This dissolves the problem four bets tried and failed to solve — every one of them proposed a new price and budgeted an hour for a billing rebuild that `pricing-constants.ts` documents as a four-part gap — and it removes the 2026-11-13 'billing live on launch day' commitment from the critical path entirely rather than rescheduling it.
theCompany:
**Muntin sells a closed month.** Not AP automation, not cost intelligence, not software: a dated, signed statement of food cost where the four legs of `Beginning + Purchases − Ending = Usage` foot on screen, every estimate is labeled, every exception carries a receipt, and any number that cannot be stood behind is withheld rather than printed. The unit of value is a deliverable with a date and a signature on it, the way an audit firm sells an opinion — not a login, not a dashboard, not a feed.

**Positioning:** "Your month closes on the second Tuesday. Every leg foots, or we withhold the number." A fixed monthly close date is a promise MarginEdge's 24-48-hour rolling turnaround structurally cannot make and one employed person can. The honesty line is not a slogan here — it is the product specification, and the seven correctness fixes are what is being bought rather than debt being deferred.

**Buyer:** the owner of a 1-3 location independent defined by vendor mix, not seat count — 8-12 active specialty vendors, zero or one broadliner. Not a guess: the 919-document corpus contains zero Sysco/US Foods/PFG invoices; its top ten are I. Halper Paper, Chefs' Warehouse, Baldor, Pat LaFrieda, Edward Don, Fresco, Montgomery County DLC, Cintas, Staples, Cozzini Bros. Champion is the bookkeeper; check-signer is the owner; the CPA is the reviewer who must not be able to dismantle the number. DMV-clustered on purpose, because marginal cost scales with distinct vendor layouts, not with invoices or customers.

**Price:** one tier. **$600/location/month, billed annually at $6,000, invoiced by hand, in the May-August seasonal peak.** Quantity = locations. No seats, no invoice quota, no trial, no SKU, no checkout surface, no GA date. Five posted prices come down and are replaced with "Pricing set at the close of the pilot." Cohort hard-capped at 10 for the pilot and ~40 ever — 40 × $600 = $288K ARR at ~13.3 founder-hours/month of close review, which is the honest one-founder ceiling and gets described as a very good one-person business rather than dressed up as a venture. The one number that decides whether it is more than that is `desk_minutes_per_close`, instrumented from customer one and published.

**Delivery:** deterministic extraction (no language model in the read path) reconciling 84-87% straight-through, plus an **agent-run exception desk under one hard constraint — the desk produces RULES, never numbers.** A session may author a vendor template, a pack-parse mapping, a catalog synonym; it may never write a quantity, a price or a total. Every rule is inspectable, replayable, and published to the customer in the close receipt. That is the honest edge of the determinism claim, disclosed in plain language on `/close/` rather than hidden behind a clever reading. It is also what the incumbents pay humans 24-48 hours to do, and it is what sets their $350 floor. The count — the real $100-150/month TCO — is not performed for the customer, it is **shrunk**: Tier-2 theoretical usage, Tier-3 pars and the fail-closed market prior derive most of the sheet, and the operator verifies only the divergent rows. Half the labor at nearly twice the sticker is the whole commercial argument, and it dies if the CPA rejects the market prior — which is why that conversation is scheduled before the price is posted.

**The storefront's job is qualification, not traffic.** At forty customers ever it needs ~400 qualified readers, and its function is to be the public audit file a bookkeeper or CPA reads for forty minutes before recommending you. New center: `/close/` (what a close guarantees, what it withholds, what it costs), `/close/specimen/` (one complete month with the exceptions shown — authorized, redacted, or from a consenting restaurant; nobody in this category publishes this), `/close/limits/` (the append-only code-cited defect register), `/cost-index/corrections/`, `/cost-index/refusals/`, and `/tools/pack-check/` — a browser-runnable tool that visibly declines to answer when the evidence is inconclusive, which is the one falsifier a stranger can actually execute. `/close/apply/` replaces all four waitlist forms: an application with five qualifying questions, because at forty customers qualification IS the funnel. The 306 cost-index pages stay, stay fresh, and are reframed as **the published basis the close is priced off** — neither the product nor the marketing, but the public half of a paid deliverable's audit trail, which is also the first functional inbound-link mechanism the 95 orphaned ingredient pages have ever had. Roughly 460 pages of explanatory prose freeze: read-only, no dated cites to re-verify, no audio, no parity ratchet. Analytics on ~50 pages, not 1,327. The measure of the storefront is not sessions; it is qualified applications and whether the CPA said yes.

**Sequencing, stated plainly.** Phase 0 (weeks 1-2, nothing else ships): the founder runs one month end to end and records four numbers; written employer authorization is obtained or the specimen moves to a consenting restaurant; the red deploy is cleared, because until it is green no agent session reaches production; the 72 flagship falsehoods are corrected and `check-src-sentinel.mjs` is wired; the data keys move to GitHub Actions secrets. Phase 1 (weeks 3-8): the seven correctness fixes, each landing with its entry in the limits register. Phase 2 (weeks 7-10): the specimen close, then two CPA/bookkeeper conversations asking exactly whether this ties to what they call food purchases and whether a market index is acceptable as a disclosed management estimate. Phase 3 (weeks 10-13): the price call, the application page, ten locations, hand-invoiced. **Traffic comes last and mostly does not come at all, because amplifying reach across surfaces that currently publish a BLS index as a $393/lb price, and a food-cost percentage biased low three ways, to a buyer whose profession is catching exactly that, converts a correctness problem into a credibility event — and credibility is the only asset this company actually has.**
verdict: Adopt price inversion as the spine — one price ($600/location/month, hand-invoiced, forty locations ever) for a signed monthly close, with correctness as the product rather than deferred debt — repaired by employer authorization before any real invoice is published, the founder's end-to-end walk moved to week one, and zero billing code for the first cohort; graft the src-sentinel/corrections program, the code-cited limits register, the browser-runnable honesty tools, and the refusals surface; and pay the honesty debt in full before amplifying a single page of reach.
